reviews.text:
App “enhancements” keep making the app worse. I wrote a VERY positive review about the app a year ago because it has changed my life in many ways - the coaching, workouts and accountability are really great. BUT a lot has changed. Pricing went way up for what they are now calling premium, which may be fair but it was a steep increase. I would be more accepting of it if the app wasn’t constantly changing for the worse. It feels that they are prioritizing design over functionality and taking away basics that are hurting the app. First and foremost, the notifications DO NOT WORK properly!! Announcement and message notifications used to open the announcement or message directly. Not anymore. Now the notifications just opens the app and you have to tap a bell icon to see a list of notifications. This makes no sense in 2025 and is such a dumb flaw. There should be fewer taps, not more. The result? I ignore all notifications rather than engaging. Secondly, the activity screen changed and I’m actually really upset about it. I used to be able to see the full week of activity progress at the top of the activity screen. I could see my walks and lifts completed and it was motivating to get my checkmarks - now it’s just gone and I can only see one day at a time. This is so incredibly frustrating!! Also, I can’t jump into a program and do a single workout and mark it complete unless I commit to the full program. This is ANOTHER inconvenience and app downgrade! It’s become so inflexible and not friendly to use. The dashboard has become essentially useless. I used to use it daily and now it’s just another screen that’s design focused, not actually functional or useful. I can’t see my week of workouts completed there or my week in review. Instead, I don’t use it at all. Lastly, tracking food - it’s been years and I still can’t simply “favorite” a food easily at the tap of an icon. Instead I have to add it as one of “my foods” or as a meal. 

I am sharing all this because I absolutely LOVED the app and now I find myself ignoring the notifications, less motivated to use it and less engaged. I wish 1stPhorm slowed down these “enhancements”, got more external user feedback and/or give users the option to view the old interface. What is happening to this app is truly disappointing.

I’ve logged out and logged back in. I’ve deleted the app and downloaded it again. I’m cleared caches. The app doesn’t save my step goals. I have to change it every day. It also gives me my unbroken walking streak badge every time I login, so it looks like I’ve earned it 112 times. 

The food logging is fine. 

I wish the tech team would figure out how to make this app better. It’s a shame because I paid for a premium membership and I’m dealing with this.

I look at fitness differently, I feel better than I ever have, and I am working toward my goals with success easier than before I joined. Great customer service, excellent product line, wonderful tailor-made advice, and someone to keep you accountable and realistic. A little tough love too! I also hate how it app doesn’t input your last weight details. I constantly use 2 Tablespoons of creamer. Myfitnesspal will remember that so when I select that item it already has the amount saved. This app does not and frequently auto defaults to the most random servings (for example chicken breast is always saved as “1 chicken breast” instead of something more common such as 4 ounces of chicken breast.

Most valuable app on my phone!. I absolutely love the 1st Phorm app it’s been a game-changer for my fitness journey and overall well-being! As someone who’s always striving to level up, this app feels like having a personal coach, nutritionist, and motivator right in my pocket, all rolled into one seamless experience.
First off, the services it provides are top-notch and incredibly comprehensive. It offers custom workout programs tailored to your goals, whether you’re into strength training, cardio, or something more specialized like CrossFit-inspired routines. I get detailed exercise videos that break down form and technique, making it easy to follow along without feeling lost. On the nutrition side, there’s robust food tracking with macro breakdowns, meal planning ideas, and even recipes that align with your dietary needs. Plus, you can connect with a real advisor or trainer for personalized guidance, join live streams for motivation, and track daily activities like steps, water intake, and sleep. The community aspect is awesome too it’s like being part of a supportive tribe that shares tips and celebrates wins.
The value here is unbeatable for the price (especially with premium access unlocking even more features like advanced coaching). It’s not just another generic fitness tracker, it’s designed for real, sustainable results without overwhelming you with ads or upsells. I’ve saved time and money by ditching multiple apps and gym memberships, and the expert-backed content feels premium, like having access to pro-level advice 24/7.
What I love most is how it empowers me to be the best version of myself. The app keeps me accountable with progress tracking and reminders, but it goes deeper by educating me on the “why” behind habits like how certain macros fuel my energy or why recovery matters. It’s shifted my mindset from quick fixes to long-term growth, helping me build strength, confidence, and discipline. Whether I’m prepping for a busy day or winding down, it aligns everything toward feeling stronger, healthier, and more vibrant. If you’re serious about transforming your life, download 1st Phorm you won’t regret it!
Now let’s talk about my trainer…
Jicky Li is a TOTAL LEGEND! Dude’s a fitness genius, dropping knowledge and always keeping it real. Super motivating, always holds me accountable, and just an awesome guy! If you want to level up, Jicky’s your man💪🔥and this is the app you need!

A good app, but not for everyone. First the good: There are a lot of advisors and from what I could tell they all have the kinds of credentials you should be looking for: Legitimate CPTs and RDs with plenty of experience under their belts. But now the bad: If you’re starting from square one like I was and now still am, there is a case for spending more to work with someone in private practice. The problem is that the advisors are basically captains of teams that have many, many members, and if you’re like me and need somebody who can critique your food logs down to the smallest details and give you 1-to-1 undivided attention…you’ll be disappointed like I was. Support team tried their best to match me up (they’ll do that if you go to their website), but the kind of personalized fit wasn’t there for me because I needed a strict focus on 1-to-1. I guess I’ll have to settle for working with my life coach instead.

MINOR EDIT: I did talk to the team member who suggested I reach out to him, but when I told him what was needed we mutually agreed that it was more than their advisors could reasonably be expected give and I really had no choice but to walk away. I still don’t think it’s a bad concept, hence the middling rating of three stars, but if you have disordered eating problems and no access to a therapist, you’re going to find the advisors here won’t fit your needs.

It was working fine outside the occasional not found from off brand products, but nearly everything scanned before the update and now hardly anything is reading.

Why can't they get this right?. When a bug fix is introduced or an improvement is made, a new bug pops up or something breaks. Some of the food database data is questionable and doesn't match what is on food labels in my pantry (for generic things like lentils). There are lots of gaps in the fitness plans--missing videos, and at least one instance in which the plan slightly changes then name of an exercise about 3 weeks in, so now you can't see your historic data for how you performed on that exercise previously (even though it's the same exercise--the workout plan thinks it's different due the slight name variation).

The quality of the content doesn't justify the cost. 1st Phorm has a lot going for it but the app stuff just isn't being executed very well.
